info.name: Material Buildroot - all HTTP APIs
info.description:
Master HTTP collection snapshot. The HTTPS companion is the HTTP surface; desktop IPC boundaries are not HTTP and are documented in docs/security/README.md.

Current integrated host actionContracts are listed by exact name and scope; structural examples remain source-authored and runtime acceptance is unverified.

Prerequisites: start the opt-in companion from the desktop with your own TLS certificate and key, trust that certificate in the client, and create a pairing challenge for the exact origin you will send. Requests must carry the exact Host authority and Origin, or they are rejected. This collection contains placeholders only; it holds no certificates, cookies, challenges, CSRF tokens or session identifiers. See docs/security/companion.md.

request.description: Copy the single-use challenge shown by the desktop into the `challenge` variable, then send. The desktop shows a native review dialog; enrollment succeeds only after that review is approved. The reply contains `csrfToken`; copy it into the current (unshared) value of `csrfToken`. The session cookie is stored by the client cookie jar and is never placed in this collection. Before pairing, choose a fresh UUID clientId and retain that exact value for X-Companion-Client; set browser to edge or chrome matching the native choice. Browser names are compatibility hints, not attestation.
Returns the current session metadata and `nextSequence`. It does not report build or connection success.

Requires scope `projects:read`. Set `sequence` to the `nextSequence` value from the previous reply. `{{$guid}}` creates a fresh UUID nonce for every send. Examples are structural templates: obtain record, file, model, revision and preview identities from actual earlier replies in the same session; placeholder IDs grant no authority.

Requires scope `builds:submit`. Set `sequence` to the `nextSequence` value from the previous reply. `{{$guid}}` creates a fresh UUID nonce for every send. Examples are structural templates: obtain record, file, model, revision and preview identities from actual earlier replies in the same session; placeholder IDs grant no authority. This is a non-read scope: the desktop must explicitly admit it. Native-confirmation-required operations still require the desktop owner to approve the actual native review; an API request cannot supply that consent. Never resend an accepted mutation after a lost reply; first reconcile actual state.
